work.text: I shall be happy if the portrait that accompanys this (of your Mother) is approved. I shall be impatien[t] to hear the Criticisms on it. … Dont be afraid that finding fault with it will have any other effect than to make me more assiduous to do better

source.author: John Singleton Copley
source.title: Copley to John Greenwood, Boston, 25 January 1771, in Letters & Papers of John Singleton Copley and Henry Pelham, 1739–1776
source.publisher: Massachusetts Historical Society (1914), via Internet Archive

work.text: John Greenwood commissioned the portrait of his mother on the occasion of her sixtieth birthday.

moment.text: I should be glad never to miss an exibition, for by it the Arts are kept in health as the Body is by Exercise.

source.author: John Singleton Copley
source.title: Copley to John Greenwood, Boston, 25 January 1771, in Letters & Papers of John Singleton Copley and Henry Pelham, 1739–1776
source.publisher: Massachusetts Historical Society (1914), via Internet Archive

moment.text: Your Picture of Mrs. Greenwood was exhibited and did great honour.

source.author: Benjamin West
source.title: Benjamin West to Copley, London, 16 June 1771, in Letters & Papers of John Singleton Copley and Henry Pelham, 1739–1776
source.publisher: Massachusetts Historical Society (1914), via Internet Archive

matters.text: I am very desirous of seeing the good Lady's Face as she now appears, with old age creeping upon her.
